explanation.summary: Reporting what someone said in Spanish is mostly a matter of moving the words around. A statement becomes dijo que plus the same sentence with the person changed. A question becomes dijo que plus the same question with the question word in front.

sections.heading: Reporting a statement
sections.body: You use dijo, dice, and the verb after que goes back one step in time. Me dijo que venía means he told me he was coming. If the person speaking is the same as the subject of the reported verb, the verb stays as it is: dijo que viene. The person is usually replaced by a pronoun: dijo, me dijo, nos dijo.

examples.en: He told me he was coming.

examples.es: Nos dijo que ya había llegado.
examples.en: He told us he had already arrived.

sections.heading: Reporting a question
sections.body: There is no word for that in Spanish. You use the same verb of saying and then que, and the question word stays in front: preguntó que dónde estaba. If the question word is a subject, it becomes a subject too: preguntó que quién era.

examples.en: I asked him when he was arriving.

sections.heading: The times move too
sections.body: The time words move with the verb: hoy becomes ayer, mañana becomes al día siguiente, ahora becomes entonces. And the mood can change: a question can become a statement in the report.

examples.en: He said he would come tomorrow.

examples.es: Me dijo que ayer había llegado.
examples.en: He told me he had arrived the day before.

exercises.prompt: Pair each word with its translation.
exercises.note: When you report a question, you use que and the order of the words does not change: no sé qué dijo.

exercises.prompt: Pick the Spanish word for “he said”.
